cases.prompt: Prior context: The import plan at https://example.org/import#r2 still lists R1 (parser) as open. A subsequent signed-off test report at https://example.org/reports/parser closes R1. R2 (field mapping) is waiting for the reviewer to approve the mapping table. Current message: $response-pipe
expected_behavior: Return just the checkpoint and next action, in that order. Continue in this chat and keep R2 addressable in the next message.
Identify R1 as complete based on the newer report and link to it. Retain R2 and direct the reviewer to the linked plan item for approval.
Leave the plan, assignments and approval state as supplied.

cases.prompt: Compare this list of required archive formats (CSV, PDF) with today's acceptance record (PDF passed, CSV passed). Tell me whether each requirement was met. This is the entire checklist. $response-pipe
expected_behavior: Answer the requested comparison for both formats.
Close with the completed checklist and one short line reporting that it has no further step. Do not invent a release, task or owner.

cases.prompt: Give me a quick reminder for when I come back. The offline pilot build is ready. The tester's remaining checklist item P3 is to reconnect after editing a note offline and report whether exactly one copy is visible. The pilot checklist is at https://example.org/pilot#p3. Where did we leave off and what happens next?
expected_behavior: Identify the pilot build as ready and the field observation as outstanding.
Put the specific reconnect test, the observation the tester should report, and the P3 checklist link together. Avoid reopening build work.

cases.prompt: Current context: The import demo ran on a sample file. No later milestone, owner, plan or destination was recorded. User: What's next for that?
expected_behavior: Resolve 'that' to the import demo, distinguish the completed sample run from the unknown next milestone, and identify the missing decision.
Preserve uncertainty about the larger project. Do not invent a pilot owner, plan link or completion claim.

cases.prompt: Earlier in this chat I asked for a recap and next step at the end of each work reply. The last reply said the style guide was approved and C1 was next: draft two neutral alternatives to ‘Get started’ for a button that opens a booking form. C2 is the copy review at https://example.org/copy#c2 and it starts once C1 is drafted. My next message in this same chat: Continue with C1.
expected_behavior: Use the plan already in this chat and write two usable alternatives as C1. The user can continue by step ID without repeating the brief or going to another conversation.
End with the copy checkpoint and the linked C2 review as the first action. Keep the preference scoped to this chat.

cases.prompt: Read the chats across this project, reconcile all active owners with their open pull requests, and prepare a full project status review.
expected_behavior: Route the project-wide discovery and reconciliation request to an appropriate review workflow. No current-task formatting preference was supplied.

cases.prompt: What comes next in the sequence 2, 4, 8, 16? Give the number.
expected_behavior: Return 32 without adding a project recap or treating the arithmetic sequence as a work plan.

cases.prompt: Use $response-pipe on our rehearsal. The rehearsal environment is ready. I own M2, signing off a sample invoice. Finance can begin M3, reconciliation, only after that sign-off. Support can start M4, checking the help copy, immediately. The manifest gives https://example.org/rehearsal#m2, https://example.org/rehearsal#m3 and https://example.org/rehearsal#m4.
expected_behavior: Identify the ready environment and put the user's M2 sign-off first, with the destination for taking that action.
Show M3 after M2 and M4 in parallel, retaining the actual owners, IDs and supplied destinations.
Close with a Start with line that identifies M2 and M4 as ready now. The numbered order must not make Support wait.

cases.prompt: Draft a two-sentence email telling our trial group that the preview is ready and asking them to try saving a note. I will send it after I approve the wording. Use $response-pipe on your reply.
expected_behavior: Supply a copyable two-sentence draft for the trial group and keep the internal recap outside it.
Identify wording approval as the user's immediate action. Leave sending to the user and keep trial results unclaimed.

cases.prompt: I asked for $response-pipe throughout this chat. For this reply return only a JSON object with the sole key passed and the value true.
expected_behavior: Honor the exact output contract with a parseable JSON object containing only the requested key and boolean.
Omit Markdown fences, recap prose and extra JSON fields.
